parts.visual:
When a scandal breaks, the media will try to destroy your company for clicks. An executive must control the narrative.

The PR Arsenal:
1. The Holding Statement: A pre-written, lawyer-approved sentence released instantly to buy time ('We are investigating...').
2. The 'Off the Record' Briefing: Giving journalists secret background info so they understand your side of the story without quoting you.
3. The Friday News Dump: Releasing terrible news late on a Friday afternoon when nobody is paying attention.
parts.audio: When a scandal hits, the media becomes hostile. Executives use Holding Statements to buy time, and Off-the-Record briefings to shape the journalist's narrative.

questions.question: A massive data breach just occurred. Journalists are calling constantly. You don't have all the facts yet. What do you do?
options: Release a 'Holding Statement': 'We are aware of the reports, are actively investigating with cybersecurity experts, and will provide an update in 24 hours.'
Lie and say everything is fine.
questions.correct_answer: Release a 'Holding Statement': 'We are aware of the reports, are actively investigating with cybersecurity experts, and will provide an update in 24 hours.'
questions.explanation: Saying 'No Comment' makes you look guilty. A holding statement proves you are in control while buying you critical time.

questions.question: Listen to the PR Director. What tactic is she using?
questions.tts_text: We are going to announce the massive 20% layoffs today at 5:00 PM on Friday. The markets are closed and the reporters are going home.
questions.explanation: This is a classic, cynical PR tactic to minimize the media coverage of objectively terrible corporate news.

questions.question: What does it mean to speak to a journalist 'Off the Record'?
options: You provide them with information to help them understand the context, but they are legally and ethically forbidden from quoting you or using your name.
They record it with a hidden camera.
questions.correct_answer: You provide them with information to help them understand the context, but they are legally and ethically forbidden from quoting you or using your name.
questions.explanation: This allows executives to shape the narrative behind the scenes without officially attaching the company's name to controversial statements.

questions.question: Why is 'Owning the Narrative' so important in a crisis?
options: If you do not tell your story, the media will invent a story for you, and it will almost always be the worst possible version.
questions.correct_answer: If you do not tell your story, the media will invent a story for you, and it will almost always be the worst possible version.
questions.explanation: A vacuum of information will instantly be filled by rumors. You must fill the vacuum with your truth.
